reasoning: The package is a standard binary AUR package that downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub repository (oetiker/mdmost) with pinned SHA-256 checksums. The PKGBUILD contains no malicious top-level code, no suspicious network operations, no obfuscation, and only performs standard file installation in package(). The .SRCINFO matches the PKGBUILD metadata. The .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml are benign configuration files. The inconclusive verdicts from two models were caused by API errors (HTTP 400 and HTTP 429), not security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified them as safe.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by API failures, not security analysis differences. Qwen3-235b encountered an HTTP 400 error when reviewing .nvchecker.toml, and openrouter/free (advisory) encountered an HTTP 429 rate limit when reviewing .gitignore. Deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed all 4 files and found them safe. The advisory report from openrouter/free does not count toward the verdict per the rules.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: API error (HTTP 400) prevented review of .nvchecker.toml
openrouter/free: API rate limit (HTTP 429) prevented review of .gitignore
learnings: API errors should not block a final verdict when other models successfully reviewed the same files. The tool should distinguish between 'could not analyze due to infrastructure failure' and 'analyzed and found suspicious'.
When multiple models review the same files and one succeeds while others fail due to API errors, the successful review should carry decisive weight if it covers all relevant files.
Consider implementing retry logic or fallback models when API errors occur, rather than marking files as inconclusive due to transient infrastructure issues.
